_meta.description: Curated offline subset of the MITRE ATT&CK Enterprise catalogue, limited to the techniques this investigation maps. Ships locally so the tool runs with no network dependency; `python -m siem_investigator --refresh-attack` reconciles these entries against the live STIX feed (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mitre/cti/master/enterprise-attack/enterprise-attack.json).

T1566.001.name: Phishing: Spearphishing Attachment
T1566.001.summary: Adversaries send emails with a malicious attachment to gain execution on a victim endpoint.

T1204.002.name: User Execution: Malicious File
T1204.002.summary: A user is induced to open a malicious file (e.g. an Office document), causing code execution.

T1059.001.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell
T1059.001.summary: Adversaries abuse PowerShell to execute commands, scripts, and payloads.

T1027.010.name: Obfuscated Files or Information: Command Obfuscation
T1027.010.summary: Adversaries obfuscate command content (e.g. base64/-enc, string tricks) to evade detection.

T1053.005.name: Scheduled Task/Job: Scheduled Task
T1053.005.summary: Adversaries create a Windows scheduled task to gain persistence or recurring execution.

T1071.001.name: Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols
T1071.001.summary: Adversaries use web protocols (HTTP/HTTPS) to blend C2 traffic with normal web traffic.

T1033.name: System Owner/User Discovery
T1033.summary: Adversaries identify the primary user or logged-on accounts (e.g. whoami).

T1087.002.name: Account Discovery: Domain Account
T1087.002.summary: Adversaries enumerate domain accounts and groups (e.g. net group "Domain Admins" /domain).

T1018.name: Remote System Discovery
T1018.summary: Adversaries enumerate other hosts/domain controllers on the network (e.g. nltest /dclist).

T1016.name: System Network Configuration Discovery
T1016.summary: Adversaries collect network configuration details (e.g. ipconfig /all).

T1082.name: System Information Discovery
T1082.summary: Adversaries gather host OS/hardware information (e.g. systeminfo).

T1003.001.name: OS Credential Dumping: LSASS Memory
T1003.001.summary: Adversaries dump LSASS memory to extract credentials (e.g. comsvcs.dll MiniDump).

T1569.002.name: System Services: Service Execution
T1569.002.summary: Adversaries execute commands by creating/starting a Windows service (e.g. PsExec / PSEXESVC).

T1021.002.name: Remote Services: SMB/Windows Admin Shares
T1021.002.summary: Adversaries use valid credentials over SMB to admin shares (C$, ADMIN$, IPC$) to move laterally.

T1078.002.name: Valid Accounts: Domain Accounts
T1078.002.summary: Adversaries use compromised domain-account credentials to access and escalate across the domain.

T1560.001.name: Archive Collected Data: Archive via Utility
T1560.001.summary: Adversaries archive collected data with a utility (e.g. 7z/rar) before exfiltration.

T1039.name: Data from Network Shared Drive
T1039.summary: Adversaries collect data from network file shares (e.g. \\host\PHI$).

T1530.name: Data from Cloud Storage
T1530.summary: Adversaries access sensitive data in cloud object stores such as Amazon S3.

T1567.002.name: Exfiltration Over Web Service: Exfiltration to Cloud Storage
T1567.002.summary: Adversaries exfiltrate data to a cloud storage service they control.

T1562.001.name: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools
T1562.001.summary: Adversaries disable or modify security tools (e.g. turning off Defender real-time protection).

T1070.001.name: Indicator Removal: Clear Windows Event Logs
T1070.001.summary: Adversaries clear Windows event logs (e.g. wevtutil cl) to remove evidence of activity.
